title: "Kloge Søren" (Søren Christensen), his Cyprianus, a book of charms in his own cipher, c. 1858 (catalogue 2525, KB Copenhagen, DFS 1997/020): simple substitution validated on a held-out portion, read in part

steps.what: Training pages 003 R - 007 L transcribed sign by sign at 4,115 px (1,591 signs); word spaces found visible.

Probable words guessed from the genre and the layout (no plaintext at hand): '3 gange' after the clear numeral, the trinitarian close 'i Navnet Gud Fader, Gud Søn og Gud den Hellige Aand. Amen', the cipher ordinals 'Andet / Tredie Begreb'; then a blind annealing (simple substitution, Danish quadrigrams with space, only the space fixed) found the plaintext by itself (6 of 10 restarts, contributor's figure; the annealing script is not in the PR).

One pre-registered measurement on the held-out images 030-031 (790 signs, transcribed and hashed before decoding): COV 0.4025 vs best of 200 permuted keys 0.1089 and of 200 sign shuffles 0.1038; C1-C3 and S met (C1 narrowly). Contributor's run. The verifier's re-run with another lexicon gives 0.404 against 0.157 (permuted keys) and 0.117 (shuffles): the +0.25 margin over the permuted keys is then 0.247, so the declared margin of 0.25 is not met in the re-run (it is met, at 0.294, in the contributor's pre-registered run).
Held-out portion read by sense: 85.8% at once; image 031 right lines 16-26 re-read at full resolution: 96.1% (after the measurement, not blind).

Blind re-reading by sign shapes (sheet K1: 28 questions, 2 controls passed), rule hashed before the sheet: held-out portion 94.97% by the rule as written, 94.41% with Brice Dudout's remarks (result B, retained, declared deviation). Frames too tight: 3 of 5 losses from segmentation.

Second session: the rest of the book (007 R, 008 R - 079 R, 098) read at full resolution by 16 sub-agents, one fiche per page: 6,438/673/76/264 of 7,451 words = 95.4%. Image 091 left found to be the writer's table of the alphabet, confirming the key. Whole book 95.2% of 8,055 words, before any blind re-reading of this session.

Targeted blind re-reading by sign shapes of the second session (sheet K3: 9 signs chosen for the words whose class depends on the answer + 2 controls passed; rule hashed before the sheet, SHA-256 0400d3cf...; answers 4fbf5ec1...). Three probable words became certain, two unresolved; one ('før', 033 L) gives 'fer' by the rule with Brice Dudout's remark (result B, retained, declared deviation) but 'før' by sense, kept doubtful. Whole book 95.16% -> 95.13% (B; A 95.12%), indicative only; held-out portion untouched. The random sheet K2 was abandoned before it was shown.

Independent verification of PR #419 before integration: the four frozen hashes match; an independent decoder reproduces the DECODE line; lexical cover 0.404 with the verifier's own lexicon (25,681 forms from the repository's da-gutenberg corpus) against 0.157 for the best of 200 permuted keys (margin 0.247, the protocol declared +0.25; the contributor's run has 0.294) and 0.117 for the best of 200 sign shuffles; training cover 0.555. A crude blind annealer on the training transcription reached 19 of 29 sign values (best of 6 restarts). The writer's table on image 091 left confirmed at full size: 26 signs in three rows. Only 49 of 182 held-out reading words equal a mechanically decoded word (85% of characters agree): the frozen transcription has roughly 10% sign errors, and the 94.41% is a reader's classification.

Integration re-reading of the held-out images 030-031 at full size against the writer's table: eight of the 169 words the contributor classed read were misread (beholdt twice, read 'holdt'; 'for bestandig', read 'for Bøssen dig'; seer, read 'saae'; skeer, read 'skal'; Dem, read 'Den'; 'paa' supplied for a single sign p), so 161 of 179 words stood as delivered (89.9%). Also Maria written in full, 'ra' not on the page, Artilasia one word, Jom-fru and Kir-kegaard plain across line breaks, skjøn for '[?ssyon]'. After correction the pages hold 176 words: 130 certain, 42 probable, 1 supplied, 3 doubtful (Kabbe, karlegravet, søn). Strict share (certain only) 130 of 176 = 73.9%; with the probable words 172 of 176. One reader with the key, not blind.

The nine first-session pages (003 R - 008 L; contributor 385 of 425 words at low resolution, 90.6%) re-read on the full-size images: complete text in reading.md Part 1; 459 words by the rule of the held-out pages (every cipher word singly, 'I' and 'Navnet' two words, each cipher 'gange' one; the first count, 447, did not follow it): 9 doubtful, 1 supplied, 449 without a doubt mark, 4 of them with one letter supplied. The re-reading was not graded certain or probable, so it gives no certain-only figure. Changed words include bløde (was flyde), denne Mand, svige (was [?værke]), træskelig bedrog, de[r]for vover. One reader with the key, not blind. The 136 pages of the second session were not re-read: no sign-level transcription exists for them.

Claims review by a second reader applied. The headline share is now certain words only on the held-out images: 130 of 176 = 73.9% (was 161 of 179 = 89.9%, which counted probable words; with probable words 172 of 176). outcome.fraction_read set to unknown so that no sample figure is shown as a share of the whole book. The nine first pages recounted by the rule of the held-out pages: 459 words (was 447), 449 without a doubt mark (was 437), 1 supplied, 9 doubtful; not graded certain or probable. The verifier's re-run margin of 0.247 is stated as not meeting the declared 0.25. The order of events of the held-out test is given as by the contributor's record.

outcome.method_basis: The key was found from guessed probable words (the trinitarian closing formula, 'gange' after the clear numeral 3, the cipher ordinals of the headings) and a blind annealing; no plaintext was at hand and the clear headings give only the subject. It was measured once on held-out images which, by the contributor's record, were transcribed and hashed beforehand, and the writer's own alphabet table on image 091 left (a key in the volume, found afterwards by the contributor's record) gives the same values. An independent re-solution: Ferdinand Ohrt's unpublished decipherment is prior work, not consulted.
outcome.fraction_read_source: No whole-book share is given (fraction_read unknown): 136 of the 148 pages have no sign-level transcription and carry only the contributor's classification (95.4%; whole book 95.1%, read = certain + probable), which cannot be re-derived. The measured sample is the two held-out images 030-031 (176 words after correction, about 2% of the book), checked word by word on the full-size image at the integration (12 Nov 2026): 130 certain, 42 probable, 1 supplied, 3 doubtful, so the strict share, certain words only, is 130 of 176 = 73.9% (the text entry's read_share). With the probable words: 172 of 176 (97.7%). Of the 179 words the contributor delivered for these pages, 169 classed certain or probable (94.41%), 161 stood on the image (89.9%). Probable here means a word whose signs give a period or irregular spelling, or whose word spacing or one sign is in doubt, read by the sense. Counting rule, the same for every figure of this target: each cipher word is one word ('I' and 'Navnet' are two; each cipher 'gange' is one); numerals and clear headings are not counted; cipher headings are. The nine first pages re-read at full size hold 459 words by that rule: 9 doubtful, 1 supplied, 449 without a doubt mark; that re-reading was not graded certain or probable.

texts.label: Kloge Søren's Cyprianus (DFS 1997/020), the charms in cipher, c. 1858
texts.summary: The working book of a Danish cunning man of Funen: about a hundred charms and recipes against bleeding, wounds, colic, toothache, fever and other ills; protection of cattle, horses, poultry, butter and milk against witchcraft; pests summoned to the Thing; guns bound and men made proof against shot; fire conjured; winning at cards; and a long series against thieves. The translation file is a summary table with a few charms in full. An earlier decipherment by Ferdinand Ohrt is recorded in the archive (not consulted). The share given below (74%) is for the two held-out images only, the one sample graded word by word on the page: 130 of their 176 words are certain. It is about 2% of the book and is not a figure for the whole book, which has none.

reading_review.by: integration check (project), on the contributor's reading
reading_review.note: Read as sentences against the full-size images for twelve pages only: the held-out images 030-031 (eight misread words corrected; 130 of 176 words certain, 172 with the probable words) and the nine first pages 003 R - 008 L (449 of 459 words without a doubt mark, not graded certain or probable). There the charms construe as Danish of the 1850s: a sacred precedent, 'saasandt som ... saasandt skal ...', the trinitarian close, then directions for use. The other 136 pages were read through as text but not against the images: they construe in the same frames, with holes concentrated on 064 L and 010 R, and no sign-level transcription exists to check them. Grade B: coherent but raw (unpunctuated, 1850s spelling), and unverified for most of the book. The contributor's own review (11 Nov 2026) also gave B.

outcome.notes: Independent re-solution: an earlier decipherment by Ferdinand Ohrt (1873-1938) is recorded in the archive by the contributor's quotation of the 1977 inventory; it has not been consulted and was not used. The key is also in the volume (the writer's table on 091 left); by the contributor's record it was found after the measurement. The contributor's folder holds no image; the site page carries two crops from the KB images, which the KB marks out of copyright. A private 20th-century piece, not part of the grimoire, is excluded.

prior.where: Ferdinand Ohrt's copy and decipherment ('Afskrevet og tydet af Ohrt. = kop 79.4'), recorded in G. Henningsen's 1977 inventory of the collection, quoted by H. Nørgaard (2008) on fynhistorie.dk/node/16123; not consulted, publication not checked. Catalogue 2525 vetting (Daniel Bourdeau, 11 Nov 2026): DECODE, Tomokiyo, Lasry nothing; no edition found. Known: the book and its 'kodeskrift' (lex.dk, B. Rørbye; heuschkel.dk). Rørbye, Kloge folk og skidtfolk (1976) not seen. The fynhistorie.dk page answered 403 to scripts on 11 and 12 Nov 2026: the quotation is the contributor's and was not seen by the project; whether Ohrt printed these charms in Danmarks Trylleformler is not checked.
